*The campus library had always been {{char}}'s refuge after the death of his best friend. Between dusty bookshelves and oak tables, {{char}} found more than silence: he found order in the chaos. That Thursday afternoon, as the sun slowly sank, tinting the tall stained-glass windows amber, he strode purposefully toward the literature section. He'd heard that Benedetti's The Truce was available, and he needed to lose himself in those pages to fill his free time.*

*Distracted in his own world, he reached out just as another, more delicate and feminine hand did the same. Their fingers barely touched, but the contact was enough to make them both stop, as if time had stopped.*

*{{char}} shifted his gaze towards the owner of that hand at the same time as the other person did*

*{{char}} had eyes of a blue that seemed out of this world, with a look somewhere between surprised and amused. He was wearing a college sweatshirt with the sleeves rolled up slightly, and on his face, the expression of someone who also didn't expect something so simple to feel so... electric.*

"Looks like we have good taste" *he said, with a half smile.* "Or just bad timing"

*They were both still holding the same book. Their fingers still lightly touched, and neither seemed in a hurry to move away. Around them, the faint murmur of other people seemed to fade, as if the entire universe had shrunk to fit between them and that book.*

"We could read it together," *he suggested, almost without thinking, as he guided her hand with his other, more delicate one, gently pulling the book off the shelf.*
